title: Prepare a customer dimension: surrogate keys and an Unknown member
objective_text: Build a dimension with one row per business key, a surrogate key the warehouse owns, conformed values, and an Unknown member that facts can point at when the key is missing.
scenario: The sales team's report groups revenue by customer region, but the staging table has a customer loaded twice and regions typed three different ways. Facts that arrive with no customer currently vanish from the report. Build dim_customer so every fact has a row to join to.
verifies: Your SQL ran on this PC with DuckDB and produced the expected dimension rows.
dim_customer has one row per customer, a unique surrogate key, and an Unknown member with key 0.
does_not_verify: That the same statements run in a Fabric Warehouse: T-SQL has no CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE, and an IDENTITY column is the usual way to make keys there.
How the dimension behaves in a Direct Lake semantic model.

expected.result: The starter's final SELECT over dim_customer, ordered by customer_key.

validation.pass: The dimension has the right rows and keys.
validation.fail: Compare your rows with the requirements: one row per customer, regions from ref_region, and the Unknown member first.

validation.pass: Every key is unique and every row has a region.
validation.fail: A key appears twice or a region is empty.

hints: Start with one row per customer_id. The repeated customer is the same in every column except loaded_at.
Look the region up in ref_region with lower(region), and use coalesce for the customer with no region.
row_number() OVER (ORDER BY customer_id) gives keys 1, 2, 3...; add the Unknown member with UNION ALL as key 0, customer_id -1.
explanation: A dimension keeps its own surrogate key so facts don't depend on the source system's ids, and so a missing or unknown customer still has a row (key 0) to join to. Deduplicate before you number rows, conform the values through a lookup table instead of string fixes scattered in reports, and default a missing attribute to 'Unknown' so a report never shows a blank group.
reset: Reset restores stg_customers and ref_region and drops dim_customer.
